detailed_description: Number Formatter previews how a number renders across nine fixed locales using the browser's Intl.NumberFormat API. Type a number, pick a style of decimal, currency, or percent, and (for currency only) pick one of five currencies: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, or CNY. The page shows a card per locale (en-US, zh-CN, ja-JP, de-DE, fr-FR, es-ES, pt-BR, ar-SA, hi-IN) with the formatted output, and clicking a card copies that value to the clipboard. Percent input is treated as a value in percent and divided by 100 before formatting. The tool does not let you add custom locales, choose accounting/compact/scientific/engineering notation, set decimal precision, batch-export results, or pick currencies beyond the five built-in options.
usage_steps: Type a number into the input box (e.g. 1234567.89)
Pick a style: decimal, currency, or percent
If currency, pick one of USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, or CNY
Read the formatted output for each of the nine built-in locales
Click any locale card to copy that formatted value to the clipboard
usage_examples: Compare how 1234567.89 formats in en-US vs de-DE vs fr-FR for a quick UI sanity check
Preview a price across the five built-in currencies before pasting one into a mockup
Render a percent value across the locale set to spot which ones use a thin space or no space
Click the Japanese card to grab the JPY-formatted string for a screenshot
